account:
There is considerable private activity around bread, grain and payment today, but I have not established anything improper. At the mill I saw eighty hay bales offered at two emeralds each. Neighbour heard the innkeeper discussing grain credit with builder and selling authorized spare planks to buy nineteen bales. I personally saw builder hand planks to baker. Neighbour says baker filled a large bread order, and a townsman reported seeing innkeeper carrying a sack of bread. Those facts suggest people are arranging supplies despite payment difficulties, but they do not prove that the grain purchase was completed.

Reports of a bridge or port change keep circulating, sometimes naming baker, innkeeper and freight. No one I questioned supplied a definite change: freight explicitly said he had verified none, and neighbour reported the same from baker. I should not treat the repeated rumour as an established policy or project.

Freight requested a ferry and warehouse operations discussion at eighteen hundred, offering to meet beforehand and escort me to the great hall. That overlaps my previously approved lighting inspection with builder, where eight lanterns were reportedly installed. Secretary protected the existing inspection and recorded the operations discussion alongside or afterward. These arrangements may simply be ordinary town business; I do not know of another purpose. The missing town account figures remain unexplained, and secretary says there are still no council letters or reliable leads identifying who holds the accounts.

Tea with neighbour was friendly, with no further verified news. I stayed too long and have reached town hall at seventeen-oh-two, late for my sixteen-thirty office appointment. Next I should check with secretary about anything missed and prepare for the eighteen-hundred inspection and operations discussion.
